subject: general
question: In which year was ‘Self Help Group – Bank Linkage Programme’ (SHG-BLP) introduced in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1992**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **1992** is the year when the 'Self Help Group – Bank Linkage Programme' (SHG-BLP) was introduced in India.
 
• The SHG-BLP is a pioneering initiative by the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) aimed at financial inclusion and poverty alleviation.
 
• This program links self-help groups (SHGs) of rural poor with the formal banking system to provide them with financial services.
 
• It has been instrumental in empowering women and promoting entrepreneurship in rural areas.
 
• The program encourages savings and provides access to credit, enabling SHG members to undertake various income-generating activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The SHG-BLP model has been recognized globally and replicated in several other countries.
 
• As of recent data, millions of SHGs have been linked to banks under this program, benefiting millions of households.
 
• The program has led to significant socio-economic development in rural areas, including improved literacy rates, better health outcomes, and enhanced social cohesion.
 
• NABARD continues to play a crucial role in the expansion and monitoring of the SHG-BLP across India.
 
• The success of SHG-BLP has also led to the introduction of other similar initiatives aimed at financial inclusion and rural development.
